sampling_model.design: The root theorem treats every allocation count \(r\in\mathcal R_{n,3}\). The accepted parent's lossless unit-symmetrization theorem maps every outcome-independent dependent labeled design to a count law \(\pi\) and uniform fixed-count conditional experiments. The local face is centered at \(q^\dagger=(1/2,1/8,3/8)\); its complement is partitioned exactly into the positive-count shells \(\mathcal S_{n,j}(M)\) and zero-count faces \(\mathcal Z_{n,A}\).
sampling_model.units: A fixed finite population of \(n\) labeled units with three binary potential outcomes; the exact response-count orbit retains all eight response types.
sampling_model.treatment: Exactly one of three arm labels is assigned to each unit, and the observation is the assigned label together with its binary outcome.
sampling_model.overlap: No overlap assumption is imposed on the unrestricted design. Interior \(n^{-1/6}\) perturbations and every zero-count boundary stratum are certified separately.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There are no superpopulation nuisances. The nonzero transverse coordinate is a least-favorable-prior device orthogonal to the finite-population contrast and is integrated through the exact orbit likelihood.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The unrestricted two-arm binary minimax risk equals \(n^{-1}-C_An^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\) and is attained by Bernoulli randomization with nonlinear shrinkage.
For the two-arm bounded-outcome game, independent assignment remains minimax when estimators are unrestricted.
Under permutation-invariant law classes and linear estimation schemes, complete randomization with Neyman allocation is minimax.
A first-order local asymptotic minimax bound applies across broad sequential experimental designs, including multiple treatments.
Pairwise-independent inclusion attains the sharp bounded-total minimax risk within the class of unbiased estimators.
Limits of experiments yield asymptotically optimal treatment rules under average and minimax risk criteria in smooth models.
Second-order minimax optimality can be characterized through positive solutions of a problem-specific Schrodinger equation.

body.tldr: The root result is a proved allocation-tube theorem for the unequal three-arm contrast \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\). For each sample-size residue it expands actual finite allocation lattices on fixed response-count and factorial-table charts, interpolates the allocation action on a canonical Freudenthal triangulation, and controls the degree-eight sequence remainder uniformly without differentiating a moving lattice or a nonintegral allocation. The exact finite-population target passes through the nonzero transverse prior and every local, dyadic exterior, and zero-count allocation stratum. The accepted parent's lossless orbit-game equality transfers the fixed-count Bayes bound to every outcome-independent dependent labeled design. Exact arithmetic remains in \(\mathbb Q(\alpha_n)\), while rational output enclosures are evaluated along the single schedules \(M_n,T_n,\varepsilon_n,G_n,\delta_n\).

project_justification.gap: The accepted parent proves the \(n^{-4/3}\) order and exact finite programs but leaves the sharp face-and-corner limit open. Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen obtain a scalar two-arm Airy expansion, and Hull's unrestricted bounded-outcome theorem is also two-arm. Neither paper supplies a nonzero transverse prior, an unequal three-arm allocation-count expansion, or a cross-sample certificate modulus.
project_justification.niche: For \(c^\dagger\), the exact response alphabet has eight types, the target and optimal full-label score have different negative-arm weights, and allocation drifts of size \(n^{-1/6}\) enter at the second-order risk scale. A scalar-path prior is exploitable by a pair-focused design, so the first nontrivial deliverable is the full unequal-three-arm tube calculation.
project_justification.fill: The project gives explicit longitudinal and transverse response measures, the finite factorial likelihood and target identity, residue-indexed finite coefficient arrays on fixed lattice charts with certified Euler--Maclaurin and uniform Stirling remainders, the parent's exact all-design orbit transfer, an exact shell-and-boundary partition, and a terminating exact-algebraic certificate whose single prescribed schedules separately budget tube, shell, action-grid, sequence, and enclosure errors.

body.related_work: Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026, Theorems 2.1--2.3, Theorem 3.1, Section 3, and Appendix C) provide the scalar two-arm reduction and Airy feedback that inform the longitudinal scaling; the root theorem instead proves an eight-type unequal-three-arm expansion with a nonzero transverse coordinate, a two-dimensional allocation face, and residue-stable finite-lattice coefficient arrays. Hull (2026, Theorem 1 and proof Steps 1--3) informs the unrestricted decision formulation but remains a two-arm coordinate-swap result. The accepted parent establishes the lossless unit-symmetrization and orbit-game equality, the first-order value, the \(n^{-4/3}\) order, and same-\(n\) rational certificate sandwiches; its equality is imported explicitly for the all-design transfer, while the strict delta is the quantified cross-sample modulus along explicit schedules for one unequal three-arm face, including every exterior shell, every zero-count face, and the random finite-population target. Bai (2023) informs related symmetry arguments under linear-estimator and invariant-law restrictions. Armstrong (2022) gives first-order efficiency bounds for broad multiple-treatment designs. Aronow and Lopatto (2026) separate marginal inclusion from pairwise dependence under unbiased estimation. Hirano and Porter (2009) inform decision-theoretic limit transfer in smooth experiments, and Levit (1986) informs the positive-solution spectral calculation. Li and Ding (2017) and Mukerjee, Dasgupta, and Rubin (2018) provide regular finite-population asymptotics and multi-treatment contrast notation. Hammer et al. (1996) supplies only the prospective complete binary-endpoint regimen-trial motivation; no censored-outcome reanalysis is claimed.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The exact \(K=3,n=3\) full-label risk \(511653/4000000\) is below the scalar Bayes lower value \(18213/136000\), but this is not evidence of an asymptotic gap. A longitudinal-only prior is also defeated by a pair-focused design. These diagnostics motivate the nonzero transverse tube and do not constitute an asymptotic theorem. Published comparator; no novelty claimed: if \(\sum_ac_a=0\), \(\sum_a|c_a|=2\), and \(|S_c|=2\), direct evaluation of the response-cost and dual-score definitions gives, after relabeling, \((c_a)=(1,-1)\), \((q_a^\star)=(1/2,1/2)\), \(V_c(v)=\kappa(c)=1\), \((\ell_a^\star)=(g_a^\star)=(1,-1)\), and \(T_i=U_i=2c_{A_i}(Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}-1/2)\). The resulting balanced independent-design expansion \(R_n^{\mathrm{ind}}(c)=n^{-1}-C_An^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\) is exactly Theorem 3.1 of Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026); it is not an application of the three-active-arm theorem.
body.honest_scope: The root theorem is confined to \(c^\dagger=(1,-1/4,-3/4)\) with fixed three-arm support and proves the allocation-tube expansion before claiming the sharp minimax consequence. Its finite-to-limit certificate uses only the displayed schedules \(M_n,T_n,\varepsilon_n,G_n,\delta_n\), exact arithmetic in \(\mathbb Q(\alpha_n)\), and rational outward enclosures; the bit complexity of those enclosures is open. No growing-arm, uniform vanishing-weight, or arbitrary-real computability claim is made. The support-two reduction remains the published scalar Airy comparator identity.
